metadata.indicator_name: Total Annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita at at constant prices in dolllars
metadata.definition:
Annual total gross domestic product (GDP) per capita at constant prices corresponds to GDP in volume terms, that is, valued at 2018 base-year prices, which makes it possible to isolate the effect of price changes and measure real economic growth, divided by the country’s total population in the corresponding year.

The population data used are not taken directly from national censuses, but from the official estimates and projections prepared by the ECLAC Latin American and Caribbean Demographic Centre (CELADE-Population Division), which harmonizes each country’s census information under a common methodology. This enhances comparability of the indicator across countries in the region, even when national censuses have different reference years or methodologies.

GDP figures are expressed in United States dollars using ECLAC’s reference exchange rate for the 2018 base year, so that currency conversion does not introduce additional distortions into the series. By fixing the exchange rate at the base-year level, changes in the indicator over time reflect changes in the volume of production per capita rather than exchange-rate movements or price effects.

Regional and subregional aggregates are calculated as the ratio of the sum of GDP for countries with available information in each period to the total population of those same countries. Consequently, the coverage of the aggregate may vary across periods depending on the availability of national series. GDP per capita represents an average level of production per person and does not reflect the distribution of income within countries.
metadata.calculation_methodology:
The region's national accounts at constant 2018 prices are obtained by back-casting and forward-extrapolating the current values of that year using the volume indices of the GDP components, calculated from the official series in national currency and applied both to the total and to each major ISIC division.

2018 is used as the base year; from there, each component is moved forward and backward according to its own volume index, which makes it possible to isolate real growth in activity from the effects of price changes.

The issue is that these indices are calculated and applied independently for total GDP and for each major ISIC division. Since the real growth of each sector doesn't necessarily move in the same proportion as the aggregate, the sum of the sectors at constant prices doesn't exactly match the total GDP obtained independently. That difference is the statistical discrepancy, and rather than forcing it to zero or distributing it arbitrarily across sectors, it's reported as a separate line in the corresponding table, following standard practice in fixed base-year, constant-price national accounts systems.

Once GDP at constant 2018 prices is obtained, it's converted to US dollars using ECLAC's reference exchange rate for that same base year, so the currency conversion doesn't introduce additional distortions into the series. To arrive at GDP per capita, that value is divided by the country's total population for the corresponding year, using the official estimates and projections from CELADE-Population Division of ECLAC, which harmonizes census data from each country under a common methodology and makes the indicator comparable across countries with censuses of different dates or methodologies. Regional and subregional totals and averages are calculated from the data available for countries reporting information for each period.
